review_candidates.title: Regional Community Stabilisation Officer (P)
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration . Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second Tier Candidates Include All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope With support from the United States Government’s (USG) Department of State Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, IOM has developed Community Stabilisation (CS) interventions in multiple countries in the West and Central Africa region. These linked large-scale initiatives seek to address under-development, social cohesion, stabilisation, and public service access challenges in post-conflict and transitioning countries with complex migration and displacement dynamics. To enhance social stability and improve access to essential services and community infrastructure, IOM will utilise an evidence-based, participatory, and area-based programming approach supported by data, analysis, and community-based planning to deliver tangible benefits to local communities in support of government. To ensure the successful launch and implementation of these initiatives, in support of Country Offices (COs), the IOM Regional Office (RO) and its Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR), the Regional Thematic Unit (RTU) will provide strategic oversight, coordination, and technical support, work closely with the CO to provide programmatic guidance, quality assurance, and operational backstopping, and ensure that interventions are aligned with IOM standards, donor requirements, and best practices. Based in the IOM RO for West and Central Africa in Dakar, Senegal, under the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD) for West and Central Africa and the direct supervision of the DHRR Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS), and in close coordination with IOM Headquarters (HQ) and IOM Global Office (GO) in Washington, DC, the Regional Community Stabilisation Officer will be responsible and accountable for monitoring and supporting the implementation and coordination of community stabilisation programming, providing technical guidance for regional coherence in methodology, implementation approach and reporting, offer technical support to IOM COs on the application of community stabilisation principles and provide recommendations to improve regional coherence, and collect, collate, and disseminate lessons learned across IOM’s community stabilisation community of practice. Responsibilities Provide technical guidance to COs on their application of IOM CS guidance and methodologies, in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Unit (DHRR-RTU) in the RO for West and Central Africa and HQ Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR). Facilitate regional coherence in implementation of cross-border CS initiatives across COs, in coordination with the DHRR-RTU, to produce a harmonised implementation approach across shared operational areas. Support IOM CO to facilitate high-level quality of deliverables by providing technical guidance and remote monitoring of programme partners’ compliance, technical advisers, programme staff, surge personnel, Implementing Partners (IP) and service providers, as needed, enabling COs to achieve consistently high-quality programme deliverables. Monitor operational, administrative and budgetary performance of regional CS initiatives and programming, identifying risks and efficiency gaps early enough to inform corrective decision-making. Analyse progress against projected expenditure forecasts and implementation plans, including collecting regular updates of implementation in the areas of intervention, drafting regular reports for the DHRR RTS to determine and propose remedial action to CO where challenges are encountered. Collaborate with IOM CO, in close coordination with the DHRR-RTU, to gather and disseminate lessons learned from community stabilisation programming, specifically in cross-border and high-instability programming contexts. Disseminate consolidated lessons learned and replicable practices more broadly across IOM’s CS Community of Practice, DHRR-RTU and regional CS project units to promote the region's contribution to global community stabilisation practice. Assist the DHRR RTS with the analysis of crisis situations, coordination, prioritisation and operational planning, and recommend areas of intervention to the DHRR-RTU, RO Operations pillar, relevant donor coordination structures and Project Committees, and to CO. Review regional reporting on community stabilisation programming, checking on required revisions and harmonisation of the monthly and interim reporting for timely submission to relevant government and donor coordination and oversight bodies. Validate the capture and contextualisation of outcome-level results, monitor lessons learned and identify challenges, bringing issues or gaps to the attention of the supervisor or relevant CO as appropriate, to safeguard the integrity of regional results reporting. Compile and produce an annual report, in close coordination with COs, on community stabilisation under CS initiatives within the region. Support the DHRR-RTU in providing capacity building, training and general support to COs implementing community stabilisation programming in the region to strengthen regional programme delivery capability. Participate in DHRR-RTU’s capacity-building activities on community stabilisation, social cohesion and peacebuilding to improve IOM staff proficiency across the region. Contribute to the development, review and implementation of complementary regional projects and multi-country community stabilisation, social cohesion, resilience and peacebuilding programmes and projects. Provide technical inputs, as requested by CO and relevant donor and government coordination bodies, to support the DHRR-RTU’s liaison with the USG representing multi-country portfolio on community stabilisation programming. Participate in relevant regional working group meetings, related fora, and other stabilisation-related events – including meetings, presentations, discussions, visits, negotiations, etc. – as requested by the DHRR RTS, to position IOM as a credible subject matter expert in regional stabilisation coordination. Undertake frequent travel to countries to provide information and support, project/programme monitoring and reporting, liaison with counterparts, and project implementation. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master's degree in International Relations, Development Studies, Development Planning, Political Science, Social Sciences, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Relevant experience in programme management in complex environments; Relevant experience in the design and implementation of area-based and community-driven approaches; Relevant experience in project implementation in crisis, post-crisis, and recovery contexts; Relevant experience in supporting government, partner, and stakeholder coordination in the domain of recovery, peacebuilding, and stabilisation; and, Relevant experience in project and program reporting. Skills Strong technical expertise in stabilisation, peacebuilding, and resilience programming; Recognised expertise in one or more of these fields: community stabilisation, community violence reduction, preventing violent extremism, local peacebuilding or social cohesion; Good verbal and written communication skills including capabilities to present to diverse audiences; Proven abilities relating to implementation (budgets, human resources, procurement, and so forth) for large-scale programming in complex environments; Thorough understanding of donor processes and regulations; and, Knowledge of financial rules and regulations. Languages For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Notes Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times. IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies .

review_candidates.description: About the Role We are seeking a seasoned Civil QA/QC Manager to oversee end-to-end quality assurance and quality control for our ongoing civil construction projects. You will lead the on-site QA/QC team, establish and enforce project quality standards, ensure full compliance with project specifications, international codes, and company quality management systems, and deliver defect-free construction outputs. This is a core leadership role that bridges technical execution, subcontractor management, and client quality acceptance. Key Responsibilities Develop, update, and implement project QA/QC plans, inspection checklists, quality procedures, and work instructions in line with ISO 9001, project specs, and industry standards. Lead and manage the on-site QA/QC team, allocate daily inspection tasks, supervise inspectors’ field work, and conduct regular team training to standardize quality execution. Oversee full-cycle civil construction quality control, including foundation works, concrete works, steel structure, backfilling, roadworks, drainage, and finishing works; conduct random and systematic on-site inspections, testing witnessing, and progress quality verification. Monitor construction quality of subcontractors, conduct regular quality audits, track non-conformities, organize root cause analysis, and drive corrective & preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate recurring quality issues. Prepare, review, and submit all QA/QC documentation, including inspection reports, test reports, material approval documents, non-conformance reports, and daily/weekly/monthly quality progress reports for client and consultant review. Coordinate with clients, consultants, project management teams, and third-party testing institutions to resolve on-site quality queries and ensure smooth quality acceptance and handover. Control material quality incoming inspection, verify material certificates, and ensure all construction materials comply with project design and specification requirements. Support internal and external quality audits, summarize project quality performance, and continuously optimize on-site quality management systems and processes. Job Requirements & Qualifications Education : Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or related engineering disciplines. Experience : 5+ years of hands-on QA/QC experience in civil construction projects, with minimum 3 years of QA/QC manager experience. Professional Knowledge : Proficient in international construction codes & standards, civil construction workmanship requirements, material testing procedures, and full set of QA/QC document management workflows. Certifications : Possession of ISO 9001 internal auditor certificate or other relevant construction quality certificates is highly preferred. Core Competencies : Strong on-site problem-solving ability, familiar with subcontractor quality management, capable of independently handling client quality inspections and audits. Language & Skill : Good English listening, speaking and writing skills (for overseas project communication); proficient in MS Office, quality report preparation and data sorting. Personal Traits : Strict, responsible, detail-oriented, with strong team management, communication and cross-department coordination capabilities.

review_candidates.description: Job Responsibilities: Establish, implement, and maintain the Project Quality Plan (PQP) on-site in accordance with ISO 9001 standards and client specifications. Conduct regular site inspections, testing, and monitoring of civil and structural works (e.g., piling, concreting, structural steel, architectural finishes) to ensure full compliance with approved drawings and methods. Coordinate and manage the Inspection and Test Plans (ITP), ensuring all requests for inspection (RFI) are raised, executed, and documented properly with consultants and clients. Issue Non-Conformance Reports (NCR) when deviations occur, and follow up closely on corrective and preventive actions (CAPA). Review material submissions, mill certificates, and third-party laboratory test reports (concrete crushing, soil compaction, etc.) to verify material compliance before deployment. Maintain comprehensive QAQC records, as-built drawings, hand-over documentation, and final QA/QC dossiers for project closeout. Liaise effectively with project managers, site supervisors, subcontractors, consultants, and client representatives on all quality-related matters. Minimum of 2–5 years of working experience in QAQC roles within the construction or infrastructure industry. (Candidates with more experience will be considered for the Senior role). Strong knowledge of local construction standards, building codes, and QAQC procedures (e.g., CONQUAS, QLASSIC quality assessment systems is a major advantage). Familiarity with ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems. Proficient in reading and interpreting technical drawings and structural blueprints. Excellent communication and report-writing skills in English and Bahasa Malaysia. Ability to speak Mandarin is an added advantage to liaise with specific subcontractors.

review_candidates.title: Project Officer
review_candidates.description: Ben jij sterk in organiseren, houd je overzicht in een dynamische internationale omgeving en krijg je energie van het ondersteunen van projecten die wereldwijd lokaal bestuur versterken? Dan is de functie van Project Officer bij VNG International iets voor jou. In deze rol zorg je ervoor dat projecten soepel verlopen, deadlines worden gehaald en projectinformatie altijd op orde is. Stap dan naar voren als Project Officer bij VNG International. Over ons VNG International is een dochterorganisatie van de Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten (VNG). Ons doel is het ontwikkelen van een krachtig en democratisch lokaal bestuur wereldwijd. Europese en internationale samenwerking tussen lokale overheden behoort nadrukkelijk tot ons werkterrein. VNG International is een bedrijf dat internationaal diensten aanbiedt aan de publieke sector veelal in opdracht van de EU, Nederlandse Ministeries, de Wereldbank, en andere nationale en multilaterale instellingen. Het hoofdkantoor is gevestigd in Den Haag waar ongeveer 50 mensen werkzaam zijn (jaaromzet 2025 ca. 41 miljoen Euro), met een dochterbedrijf in Tunesië. Voor het uitvoeren van de werkzaamheden binnen de projecten (op locatie) maken we gebruik van een groot netwerk van experts op relevante vakgebieden. Kort samengevat is valt ons werk te verdelen in de volgende activiteiten: Managen van internationale projecten in opdracht van het Nederlandse Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken, de EU en de Wereldbank ter versterking van het lokaal bestuur wereldwijd. Ondersteunen van Nederlandse gemeenten bij de ontwikkeling van hun Europese en internationale beleid, en hoe ze optimaal gebruik kunnen maken van Europese fondsen en kennisnetwerken. Ondersteunen van Nederlandse gemeenten bij het werken aan de mondiale duurzame ontwikkelingsdoelstellingen van de VN: de Global Goals for Sustainable Development (SDG’s). Acquireren van internationale projecten. Wat ga je doen? Als Project Officer ondersteun je meerdere internationale projecten van begin tot eind. Je vervult een belangrijke coördinerende en administratieve rol en zorgt ervoor dat projectactiviteiten, processen en projectinformatie efficiënt en zorgvuldig worden georganiseerd. Je organiseert studie- en werkbezoeken samen met de Events Officer, ondersteunt de inzet van experts en bereidt project overleggen voor. Daarbij bewaak je actiepunten, planningen, deadlines en de voortgang van werkzaamheden. Je houdt toezicht op de tijdige oplevering van rapportages en ondersteunt bij o.a. voortgangsrapportages en projectevaluaties. Daarnaast ben je verantwoordelijk voor een correcte en actuele projectadministratie. Je verwerkt projectgegevens in de daarvoor bestemde systemen, beheert en archiveert projectdossiers en bewaakt de kwaliteit, volledigheid en toegankelijkheid van projectdocumentatie. Ook ondersteun je bij contractbeheer, verzorg je de administratieve opvolging van projectactiviteiten en zie je toe op de naleving van interne procedures en afspraken. Een belangrijk onderdeel van de functie is het ondersteunen van financiële en administratieve processen. Je controleert en verwerkt ingediende facturen en declaraties, coördineert goedkeuringsprocessen en zorgt voor een juiste en tijdige administratieve afhandeling. Tot slot signaleer je afwijkingen of knelpunten en draag je bij aan de verbetering van werkprocessen en projectondersteuning. Het team De Project Officer maakt onderdeel uit van het team Programmes, dat bestaat uit in 18 tot 20 medewerkers en wordt aangestuurd door de Manager Programmes. Binnen het team wordt nauw samengewerkt aan de voorbereiding, uitvoering, monitoring en administratieve ondersteuning van uiteenlopende projecten. In deze rol ondersteun je gelijktijdig meerdere projecten en werk je daarbij samen met verschillende (Senior) Project & Account Leads en Project Managers. Voor de inhoudelijke uitvoering van de project ondersteunende werkzaamheden rapporteert de Project Officer per project aan de verantwoordelijke Project & Account Lead of Project Manager. Wat bieden we jou? In de rol van Project Officer krijg je de kans om een directe bijdrage te leveren aan internationale projecten die maatschappelijke impact maken en lokaal bestuur wereldwijd versterken. Je vervult een afwisselende functie waarin je samenwerkt met collega’s, experts, partners en opdrachtgevers uit verschillende landen en culturen. Daarbij maak je deel uit van een internationaal netwerk en werk je mee aan projecten die ertoe doen. Je krijgt een contract voor 12 maanden , met uitzicht op verlenging bij goed functioneren en gelijkblijvende bedrijfsomstandigheden. Jouw salaris valt tussen schaal 7 en schaal 9 en bedraagt tussen € 3035,00 bruto en € 4674,00 bruto per maand op basis van een 40-urige werkweek. De uiteindelijke inschaling is afhankelijk van jouw opleiding en werkervaring. Daarnaast ontvang je 8% vakantiegeld en een eindejaarsuitkering van 4,6% vast en 3,4% variabel. Ook krijg je een volledige reiskostenvergoeding met een NS Business Card. Bij VNG International is altijd ruimte om samen te kijken naar mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen . Je werkt hybride en krijgt de ruimte om zelf te bepalen hoe je je werkdag invult. Ben je op kantoor? Dan werk je in een mooie werkomgeving in een monumentaal pand; de Willemshof. Daarnaast kun je rekenen op goede lunchopties in ons bedrijfsrestaurant. Over jou Je voelt je thuis in een ondersteunende projectomgeving waarin verschillende werkzaamheden en deadlines gelijktijdig aandacht vragen. Met een gestructureerde en nauwkeurige werkwijze bewaak je de voortgang van werkzaamheden en signaleer je tijdig mogelijke knelpunten of afwijkingen. Je neemt initiatief om passende acties in gang te zetten en draagt daarmee bij aan een efficiënte en kwalitatieve projectuitvoering. Daarnaast werk je constructief samen met collega's, internationale partners en andere stakeholders en zorg je voor een heldere en tijdige informatievoorziening. Dankzij je sterke communicatieve vaardigheden ben je in staat om effectief te schakelen tussen verschillende doelgroepen en uiteenlopende administratieve, organisatorische en inhoudelijke werkzaamheden. Wat neem je mee? Een afgeronde mbo-4- of hbo-opleiding in een relevante richting, zoals projectmanagement, bedrijfskunde, business support, bedrijfsadministratie of internationale betrekkingen. Ervaring met of aantoonbare affiniteit voor projectmatig werken in een ondersteunende rol. Je beschikt over ervaring in administratieve en organisatorische processen en weet projecten effectief te ondersteunen. Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse (C2 niveau) en Engelse taal, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Beheersing van de Franse taal is een pré. Het vermogen om zelfstandig te werken binnen afgesproken kaders en tegelijkertijd effectief samen te werken met verschillende interne en externe stakeholders. Bij VNG International hechten we waarde aan het vergroten van diversiteit binnen de organisatie. Verschillende perspectieven, achtergronden en inzichten vergroten onze denkkracht en handelingsperspectieven. Ook als je jezelf niet 100% herkent in de gevraagde kenmerken van de functie, nodigen we je van harte uit om te solliciteren. Jouw persoonlijke ervaringen en/of levensverhaal kunnen behulpzaam zijn om buiten de kaders te denken Stap naar voren: solliciteer direct Ben jij de initiatiefrijke Project Officer die we zoeken? Solliciteer hier, vóór 4 november . Voor vragen kan je terecht bij Janice Ranty, HR Business Partner; Janice.Ranty@vng.nl VNG International zoekt zelf haar kandidaten, aanbiedingen van derden worden niet op prijs gesteld.

Text WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The EU Intelligence and Situation Centre (EU INTCEN) is the exclusive civilian intelligence centre of the EU, providing in-depth analysis for decision makers in all EU Institutions. As such, EU INTCEN is a directorate of the EEAS that is directly attached to the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and Vice-President of the European Commission. It comprises an Intelligence Analysis Division (INTCEN.1) and a Support/Open-Source Research Division (INTCEN.2). EU INTCEN also offers its services to the various EU decision-making bodies in the fields of the EU Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), Common Security Defence policy (CSDP) and Counter Terrorism, as well as to the Member States. Under the Single Intelligence Analysis Capacity (SIAC) agreement, it works hand in hand with its military counterpart, the EUMS INT, in order to deliver joint civilian and military intelligence assessments. The Support/Open-Sources Research Division supports the Intelligence Analysis Division of EU INTCEN and EUMS Int by providing open-source intelligence from monitoring, collecting and assessing Open-Source information, political and diplomatic reporting, using advanced research and analytical tools and services. Doing so, INTCEN 2 complements and broadens the material and analytical basis for the Intelligence output of INTCEN and EUMS Int. WE PROPOSE The position of open-source intelligence analyst - contract agent FGIV as per Article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). The Open-Source Intelligence Analysist will collect, research, monitor and analyse open-source information including from social media, as well as political and diplomatic reporting. He/she will analyse open-sources and draft open-source intelligence reports in order to provide input to intelligence-based reports. The Contract agent will support the work of dedicated INTCEN and SIAC Task Forces. The contract agent will also be requested to monitor the political, economic, military and/or humanitarian situation in selected countries/regions. He/she will produce Open-Source information research in support of customers within the Single Intelligence Analysis Capacity (SIAC) of the EEAS. The Contract Agent will be part of an INTCEN.2 team and will work in close association with the Intelligence Analysts of INTCEN's Intelligence Analysis Division and EUMS Int. division. Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group IV), as per Article 3b of the CEOS, on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year. This contract may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: 15/01/2027 LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof. WE LOOK FOR Skills A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good research, analytical, IT, and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Research and collect Open-Source information using automatised open-source research Analyse Open-Sources on global issues and/or geographical issues in order to provide input to INTCEN/SIAC reports Prepare analysis reports on global and security threats and geographical issues in support of intelligence work of SIAC Monitor and provide updates on specific global and geographical issues. Eligibility criteria In Addition To The Conditions Set Out In Article 82 Of The CEOS And In The Commission Decision C(2017) 6760 Final , Which Is Applicable To The EEAS By Virtue Of The Decision ADMIN(2018) 4 Of The High Representative, Candidates Must have passed a valid EPSO CAST in FG IV, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST for FG IV (https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration). Selection criteria Candidates Should Have have strong capacity to analyse and structure information and excellent drafting skills combined with sound judgement; have an excellent knowledge of internet, social media and IT tools and be able to carry out research using those tools; knowledge of external relations, internal policies and functioning of the Union; have a strong sense of organisation and experience in collecting and analysing information; have knowledge and/or experience of global security threats and issues, and of external relations; have the ability to communicate clearly on complex issues and the capacity to perform with accuracy and in a flexible manner a diversity of tasks in a complex institutional environment; be a flexible team player; strong service attitude; have the ability to work both independently and in a team, under pressure and tight deadlines and respond to changes in a potentially rapidly evolving environment. Furthermore experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience of working in Open-Source Intelligence (including social media); experience in using tools related to Open-Source Intelligence; knowledge and experience in MENA region; will be considered as strong assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest (see attached). MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS. Given the specific role of the INTCEN and the sensitive nature of the tasks pertaining to the offered position which requires candidates to have already gained an experience in handling EUCI documents, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) issued by the competent authority of their Member State in accordance with national laws and regulations is mandatory at the moment of application in order to enter the selection process. The selected candidate may still be required to obtain a new PSC for the present post in accordance with national laws and regulations of his or her Member State and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS.
